proposals.before: Qing Bu rebelled and fled. Han established imperial son Chang as King of Huainan, and Zhang Cang served as his chancellor.
proposals.after: Qing Bu rebelled and was destroyed. Han established imperial son Chang as King of Huainan, and Zhang Cang served as his chancellor.
proposals.reason: In 黥布反亡, 亡 means he perished/was destroyed after rebelling, not that he fled; the idiomatic already renders this correctly.

proposals.before: He was then transferred once more to serve as Chancellor of Dai.
proposals.after: He was then transferred once more to serve as chancellor to the King of Dai.
proposals.reason: Chinese 相代王 names the Dai king as the person served; the idiomatic omits that titled referent present in the source and literal.

proposals.before: Zhou Chang laugh say;
proposals.after: Zhou Chang laughed and said,

proposals.after: I privately worry about it, and do not know what to do."

proposals.after: Yao said, "Your Majesty should alone establish for the King of Zhao a noble and powerful chancellor, and only one whom Empress Lu, the crown prince, and the ministers have always revered and feared will do."
proposals.reason: Literal English is broken and obscures the counsel.

proposals.after: Yao said, "Censor Grand Master Zhou Chang is firm, enduring, simple, and upright; moreover Empress Lu, the crown prince, and the great ministers have all always revered and feared him."

proposals.before: After three years he was dismissed, and Pingyang marquis Cao Jiu was made Censor Grand Master.
proposals.after: After three years he was dismissed, and Cao Zhu, Marquis of Pingyang, was made Censor Grand Master.
proposals.reason: The personal name 窋 is Zhu, matching the idiomatic translation; the revision also restores natural English title order.

proposals.before: In the fifth year before the reign of Emperor Jing, Cang died and was posthumously honored with the title Marquis Wen.
proposals.after: In the fifth year of Emperor Jing's former reign period, Cang died and was posthumously honored with the title Marquis Wen.
proposals.reason: 孝景前五年 means Former Era year 5 of Emperor Jing (152 BC), not a year before his reign began.

proposals.before: In the fifth year before Xiaojing's reign, Cang died, posthumously titled Marquis Wen.
proposals.after: In Xiaojing's former fifth year, Cang died, posthumously titled Marquis Wen.
proposals.reason: 前 marks the former reign-period designation, not chronological priority before the reign.

proposals.before: Initially, Zhang Cang's father was not full five chi in height. When he gave birth to Cang, Cang was over eight chi tall, and became marquis and chancellor.
proposals.after: Initially, Zhang Cang's father was not full five chi in height. When Cang was born, Cang was over eight chi tall, and became marquis and chancellor.
proposals.reason: 及生蒼 means when Cang was born; the father did not give birth.

proposals.before: Zhang Cang was virtuous to Wang Ling.
proposals.after: Zhang Cang was indebted in virtue to Wang Ling.
proposals.reason: 德 here means felt grateful/indebted for kindness received, not that Cang behaved virtuously toward Ling.

proposals.before: Guangguo was worthy and had good conduct, so he wished to make him chancellor. After thinking about it for a long time, he decided it was not possible. Moreover, the great ministers from Gao emperor's time had mostly died, and there were no suitable ones remaining. So he made Censor Grand Master Jia chancellor, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Guan according to his old fief.
proposals.after: Guangguo was worthy and had good conduct, so he wished to make him chancellor. After thinking about it for a long time, he decided it was not possible. Moreover, the great ministers from Gao emperor's time had mostly died, and there were no suitable ones remaining. So he made Censor Grand Master Jia chancellor, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Gu'an according to his old fief.
proposals.reason: 故安侯 is Gu'an, not Guan; the idiomatic rendering already has Gu'an.

proposals.before: Until court of ritual, not can not solemn!"
proposals.after: As for the rites of court, they cannot but be kept solemn!"
proposals.reason: Literal English is ungrammatical and obscures 不可以不肅.

proposals.before: Afterwards, a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji. Then Emperor Wen summoned Gongsun Chen to serve as doctor, drafted the calendar system for earth virtue, and changed the first year.
proposals.after: Afterwards, a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji. Then Emperor Wen summoned Gongsun Chen to serve as erudite, to draft the calendar system for earth virtue, and changed the first year.
proposals.reason: 草土德之歷制度 is Gongsun Chen's charge; the English makes Emperor Wen the drafter, and 博士 is Erudite not medical doctor.

proposals.before: Chancellor You Che was a man from Changling.
proposals.after: There was Chancellor Che, who was a man from Changling.
proposals.reason: Chinese 有車丞相 means 'there was Chancellor Che'; the literal wrongly takes 有 as a surname You.

proposals.before: Chancellor Wei was a worthy man, a person from Lu.
proposals.after: Chancellor Wei Xian was a person from Lu.
proposals.reason: 韋丞相賢者 uses 賢 as the personal name Xian, not the adjective 'worthy'.

proposals.before: At that time Jing Zhao prefect Zhao Jun was memorialized by the chancellor to be exempted from crime. He sent people to arrest Chancellor Wei, wishing to seek escape from crime, but Wei did not listen.
proposals.after: At that time the Prefect of the Capital, Zhao Jun, was memorialized by the chancellor for removal on criminal charges. He sent men to seize Chancellor Wei, hoping to escape punishment, but Wei would not yield.
proposals.reason: Context shows Zhao facing punishment and then coercing Wei to escape guilt; 奏以免罪 here is dismissal/punishment, not exemption from crime.

proposals.before: Grant the rank of Guan Nei marquis, one hundred catties of yellow gold.'
proposals.after: He was granted the rank of Marquis Within the Pass and one hundred catties of yellow gold."
proposals.reason: Literal English drops the passive grant subject, leaves a mismatched quote mark, and transliterates 關內侯 instead of rendering the noble title.

proposals.before: Censor Grand Master Xue Jun was exempted, and he became Censor Grand Master.
proposals.after: Censor Grand Master Xue Jun was dismissed, and he became Censor Grand Master.
proposals.reason: 免 here means dismissal from office, not exemption; 'exempted' reverses the administrative sense.

proposals.before: His talent descended, he shot at the policy questions several times without hitting, until the ninth time, then he hit the Bing grade.
proposals.after: His abilities were mediocre; he sat the policy examinations several times without passing, and only on the ninth attempt did he achieve the third-class grade.
proposals.reason: 才下 means mediocre ability, not that talent 'descended'; the archery metaphor also obscures the examination sense of 射策.

proposals.before: He supplemented as Pingyuan literature graduated secretary.
proposals.after: He was appointed as a Literary Clerk in Pingyuan commandery.
proposals.reason: 文學卒史 is the office Literary Clerk; 'literature graduated secretary' and 'supplemented as' are opaque calques.

proposals.before: Xiaoyuan was fond of Poetry, so he was moved to be Guanglu Xun, dwelling in the palace as teacher, teaching and instructing those on left and right, while county officials sat by his side listening, very much praising it, daily becoming more honored and noble.
proposals.after: Xiaoyuan was fond of the Poetry, so he was moved to be Superintendent of the Imperial Household, dwelling in the palace as teacher, instructing those around him, while the sovereign sat by his side listening, regarding it very highly, and he grew more honored by the day.
proposals.reason: 縣官 here means the emperor/sovereign, not 'county officials'; 光祿勳 should be rendered as the office title rather than bare transliteration.

proposals.before: Censor Grand Master Zheng Hong was exempted for matters, and Gentleman Kuang became Censor Grand Master.
proposals.after: Censor Grand Master Zheng Hong was dismissed for misconduct, and Gentleman Kuang became Censor Grand Master.
proposals.reason: 坐事免 is dismissal for an offense; 'exempted for matters' misreads both 免 and 坐事.

decisions.reason: 亡 describes Qing Bu's destruction after his rebellion, not his flight; the idiomatic translation already preserves the event correctly.

decisions.after: He was then transferred again to serve as chancellor to the King of Dai.
decisions.reason: 相代王 identifies the King of Dai as the ruler Zhang Cang served; the revised wording makes that relationship explicit in natural English.
The proposal turns the telegraphic calque into grammatical English without changing the attribution.
The Chinese closes the speech here, so the mismatched single quotation mark should be corrected to a double quotation mark.

decisions.after: Yao said, "Your Majesty should appoint a noble and powerful chancellor for the King of Zhao, one whom Empress Lu, the crown prince, and the ministers have always revered and feared. Only such a man will do."
decisions.reason: The source calls for a powerful chancellor whom the court fears and respects; this keeps every element while avoiding the proposal's awkward 'should alone establish.'

decisions.reason: The proposal correctly repairs the prose, but the quotation must remain open because Yao's answer concludes in s0062.
The proposal restores natural word order and correctly closes the speech that began in s0061.
The proposal correctly joins Gaozu's name and supplies a grammatical speech tag and quotation.
窋 is Zhu, and the proposed English title order is both accurate and idiomatic.

decisions.after: In the fifth year of Emperor Jing's first reign period (152 BC), Cang died and was posthumously honored with the title Marquis Wen.
decisions.reason: 前五年 is the fifth year of Emperor Jing's first chronological period, not five years before his reign; adding 152 BC makes the date unambiguous in English.

decisions.after: In the fifth year of Xiaojing's first reign period, Cang died and was posthumously titled Marquis Wen.
decisions.reason: The literal translation must treat 前 as the first of Emperor Jing's numbered reign periods, not as a time before his accession.

decisions.after: At first, Zhang Cang's father was less than five chi tall. Yet the son he fathered, Cang, grew to over eight chi tall and became a marquis and chancellor.
decisions.reason: The father did not give birth, but the proposal could also imply that Cang was eight chi tall at birth; this wording preserves the contrast and later growth.

decisions.after: Zhang Cang was grateful to Wang Ling.
decisions.reason: 德 here means that Zhang Cang felt gratitude for Wang Ling's kindness; 'indebted in virtue' is accurate in direction but unnatural English.

decisions.after: Guangguo was worthy and upright, so the emperor wished to make him chancellor. After long deliberation, however, he decided it was impossible. Most of the senior ministers from Emperor Gao's time had already died, and none of those remaining appeared suitable. He therefore made Censor Grand Master Jia chancellor and, on the basis of his former fief, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Gu'an.
decisions.reason: 故安 is Gu'an, and the surrounding literal prose also benefits from grammatical subjects and natural official-title phrasing.
不可以不肅 is an emphatic requirement that court rites be solemn; the proposal renders it clearly and closes the speech correctly.

decisions.after: Afterward, a yellow dragon appeared at Chengji. Emperor Wen then summoned Gongsun Chen, appointed him an Erudite, ordered him to draft a calendar and institutions based on the virtue of Earth, and inaugurated a new first year.
decisions.reason: 博士 is Erudite, and Emperor Wen remains the subject who appoints Gongsun Chen, orders the drafting, and inaugurates the new calendar.
